title: Planning a Girls Trip to Rwanda? Gorillas, Kigali Cafés and a Lazy Lake Kivu Finish
meta_title: Girls Trip to Rwanda Planner: Route, Permits and Costs
meta_description: Plan a girls trip to Rwanda: a 7-day route through Kigali, the gorillas and Lake Kivu, permit prices, rooming and costs per person for your group.
excerpt: A girls trip to Rwanda fits gorillas, Kigali's cafés and a Lake Kivu finish into one easy week. Here is the route, the permits and what it costs your group.
content:
A girls trip to Rwanda packs mountain gorillas, a buzzing capital and a lakeside finish into one compact week. Seven days usually covers two nights in Kigali, two or three near Volcanoes National Park and two on Lake Kivu, with short, paved drives between them and one private guide looking after the whole group.

The tricky part is not choosing Rwanda; it is fitting six friends with different budgets, fitness levels and ideas of a good holiday into one plan. This guide sets out the route, the permits, the real costs and the little logistics that make a friends' trip work, and shows how our special occasion safaris team in Nairobi builds a private trip around your crew.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 7 days; 5 for Kigali and gorillas only, 9-10 to add Akagera or Nyungwe
  • Group size: 4 to 6 friends share one vehicle; 7 to 12 need two vehicles or a minibus
  • Gorilla permit: US$1,500 per foreign adult, minimum age 15, up to 8 visitors per gorilla family a day (checked November 2026)
  • Golden monkeys: US$100 per foreign adult in Volcanoes National Park (checked November 2026)
  • Kigali to Musanze: About 2.5 hours by road
  • Driest months: June to September and mid-December to February
  • Visa: Visa on arrival; fee waived for African Union, Commonwealth and Francophonie citizens, capped at US$50 for others (checked November 2026)

Is Rwanda a Good Destination for a Trip With Friends?

A girls trip to Rwanda works because the country is small, safe by regional standards and varied. In one week you can trek to gorillas, spend an evening in rooftop bars and cafés, and laze by a freshwater lake, without a single long internal flight or a bumpy all-day drive.

A girls trip to Rwanda suits groups who want more than a game drive. A classic Kenya or Tanzania safari is built around the vehicle, while Rwanda mixes a mountain hike, culture, food and design with its wildlife. That variety helps when one friend lives for animals and another mainly wants good coffee, a market and a sunset drink.

The honest trade-offs of a girls trip to Rwanda are cost and pace. Gorilla permits are expensive, the best lodges near the volcanoes fill months ahead, and the big-game safari in Akagera is good but less dense than the Masai Mara. Groups whose main wish is lions, cheetahs and the migration should look at our girls trip to Kenya instead, or pair the two countries.

Why a private girls trip to Rwanda beats joining a tour

A private girls trip to Rwanda means your own vehicle, guide and timetable. Nobody waits for strangers at breakfast, the music and the stops are yours, and you can swap a museum for a spa afternoon on the day. It also lets the group split easily: trekkers head to the forest while others take a slower morning, then everyone meets for lunch.

How Many Days Do You Need, and What Does the Route Look Like?

Seven days is enough for most girls trips to Rwanda: Kigali, Volcanoes National Park and Lake Kivu, each with at least two nights. The loop starts and ends at Kigali International Airport, so friends flying in from different cities can meet in the capital and leave on separate evening flights.

DayWhereWhat the group does
Day 1KigaliArrive, check in, sunset drinks and dinner together
Day 2KigaliKigali Genocide Memorial in the morning, markets, an art centre and cafés in the afternoon
Day 3Kigali to MusanzeDrive about 2.5 hours north, lunch with volcano views, a short village walk or spa time
Day 4Volcanoes National ParkGorilla trek for those aged 15 and over; non-trekkers take a cultural visit or rest
Day 5Volcanoes to Lake KivuGolden monkey tracking in the morning, then about 1.5 hours to Rubavu on the lake
Day 6Lake KivuBoat trip, kayaking, coffee farm visit or a full lazy day
Day 7Rubavu to KigaliDrive back to Kigali for a final lunch and evening flights

A five-day girls trip to Rwanda drops Lake Kivu and runs Kigali, two nights at the volcanoes and back. A nine- or ten-day version adds two nights in Akagera for a savannah safari, or two in Nyungwe Forest for chimpanzees and the canopy walk. Our 6-day Rwanda wildlife, culture and Lake Kivu holiday follows a gentler route without gorillas, which suits friends who would rather spend the permit money elsewhere.

What Should Friends Do in Kigali?

On a girls trip to Rwanda, Kigali deserves two nights, not a quick stop. A morning at the Kigali Genocide Memorial gives every later conversation in Rwanda its context, and afternoons in markets, galleries and cafés show how lively and creative the city is today. Evenings are for long dinners and rooftop views over the hills.

The Kigali Genocide Memorial is free to enter and open 9:00 to 17:00 daily, with last entry at 16:00; on the last Saturday of each month it opens only from 13:00 because of Umuganda community work. An optional package with an audio guide costs about US$30 per international visitor, children under 12 are not admitted, and photography inside the museum is not allowed (all from the memorial's visitor guidance, checked November 2026).

After the memorial, most groups on a girls trip to Rwanda unwind with a mix of Kimironko Market for fabric and baskets, an art centre or two, a walk through the Nyamirambo neighbourhood and a Rwandan coffee tasting. Many friends love having a dress made from local fabric by a tailor, so plan that on day one if you want it collected before you leave.

Good to know before a night out

Kigali is relaxed but tidy and quite conservative in dress, so smart-casual works everywhere. Rwanda bans plastic bags, so pack shopping in cloth or paper. Ride-hailing and metered taxis are easy in the city, but we keep your guide on call for late evenings so the group always gets back together.

Gorillas and Golden Monkeys in Volcanoes National Park

Volcanoes National Park is the heart of any girls trip to Rwanda. Each trekker needs a gorilla permit of US$1,500 per foreign adult (checked November 2026), must be at least 15, and joins a group of no more than eight people who spend one hour with a habituated gorilla family. Permits are personal and booked in advance.

Treks start with a briefing at the Kinigi park headquarters around 7:00. The walk to the gorillas can take anything from under an hour to three or more each way, on steep, muddy farmland and bamboo, and rangers match families to fitness. If one of your friends is nervous about the climb, our guide to how hard gorilla trekking is explains how to ask for an easier family and when to hire a porter.

Golden monkey tracking costs US$100 and is the best second activity on a girls trip to Rwanda: shorter, playful and great for photos. The Dian Fossey tomb hike and the Mount Bisoke climb cost about US$75 each per foreign visitor (checked November 2026). Our posts on the Rwanda gorilla permit and golden monkey trekking in Rwanda cover booking and discounts in detail.

Planning a girls trip to Rwanda around one gorilla family

Because each family takes eight visitors, a group of up to eight can usually trek together if permits are booked early. Larger groups trek to two families at the same time and swap stories at lunch. In June to September and over Christmas, permits and the best lodges near Kinigi go first, so a deposit four to six months ahead is wise.

Why Finish on Lake Kivu?

Lake Kivu is the reward on a girls trip to Rwanda after the early starts and muddy boots. Rubavu, about 1.5 hours from Musanze, has a palm-lined shore, lakeside hotels with pools and calm water for kayaking, so the group can spend two slow days together before heading home.

Typical Lake Kivu days include a boat trip to the islands, a morning paddle, a visit to a coffee washing station in the hills and long lunches by the water. Health advice warns travellers to avoid swimming in fresh water in Rwanda because of bilharzia, so most groups swim in hotel pools and enjoy the lake from a boat. For a deeper look at the shore towns, read our Lake Kivu retreat guide.

Should You Add Akagera or Nyungwe?

On a longer girls trip to Rwanda, Akagera suits groups who want a classic game drive with lions, elephants and a boat trip among hippos, while Nyungwe suits groups who want rainforest, chimpanzees and the canopy walkway. Each needs two nights, so choose one unless your trip runs ten days or more.

Nyungwe charges foreign non-residents US$100 park entry for one night, chimpanzee tracking at US$150 (age 15 and over) and the guided canopy walk at US$40, according to the park's 2025-2026 price list (checked November 2026). The canopy walk is a fun group challenge, swaying above the trees, and does not need much fitness.

Akagera lies about 2.5 hours east of Kigali. Its published tariff lists park entry at US$100 per international visitor for one day or night, a scheduled boat trip from about US$35 per person and a sunset boat trip at about US$45 (checked November 2026). It works best at the start of the trip, straight from the airport, before you head north to the volcanoes.

How Much Does a Girls Trip to Rwanda Cost?

A seven-day girls trip to Rwanda costs roughly US$3,000 to US$6,500 per person in mid-range hotels and US$9,000 or more in luxury lodges, sharing rooms and a vehicle. The gorilla permit alone is US$1,500, a big share of any budget.

StyleWhat you get7 days per person (estimate)
Comfortable mid-rangeGood city hotel, comfortable lodge near the park, lakeside hotel, private vehicle and guide, one gorilla trekUS$3,000-4,000
Upper mid-rangeBoutique Kigali hotel, well-known lodges near Kinigi and on Lake Kivu, gorillas and golden monkeysUS$4,500-6,500
LuxuryTop-tier lodges near the volcanoes, private villa-style rooms, gorillas, golden monkeys and spa timeUS$9,000+

These girls trip to Rwanda figures are estimates per person, sharing twin or double rooms in a group of four to six, with park fees, meals on safari and the vehicle included but international flights, visas, drinks and tips excluded. Single rooms add a supplement, and a group of three or four pays more each for the vehicle than a group of six.

Rooms, vehicles and paying separately

Friends on a girls trip to Rwanda often want a mix of twin rooms and one or two singles, and lodges near the park are small, so we hold rooms early and can split a larger group between two lodges of the same standard. On our 6-day Rwanda celebration safari, every seventh place is free for each six paying travellers, each person can pay separately, and friends can fly in on different flights.

On any girls trip to Rwanda, up to six friends fit one safari vehicle with window seats for everyone. Seven to twelve travel in two vehicles or a minibus, which works well on Rwanda's mostly paved roads. Our page on how to organise a group safari explains deposits, rooming lists and how we handle late joiners.

Insider Tips

  • Book permits first: Secure gorilla permits before flights in June-September and at Christmas
  • Name one organiser: One friend collects passport details and rooming wishes, which keeps permits and lodges accurate
  • Pack for the trek: Waterproof jacket, gloves for nettles, ankle boots and long trousers; see our gorilla trekking packing list
  • Visa check: Most nationalities get a visa on arrival, and the East Africa Tourist Visa helps if you add Kenya
  • Plan Umuganda: On the last Saturday of the month, shops and roads are quiet until about midday
  • Leave a free afternoon: A spa hour, tailor fitting or simply a nap makes the week feel like a holiday

Rwanda's immigration service confirms that visitors of every nationality can get a visa on arrival, with the fee waived for African Union, Commonwealth and La Francophonie citizens on a 30-day visit; check the official visa on arrival page before you fly. Frequently Asked Questions

Is Rwanda safe for a girls trip?

Yes, a girls trip to Rwanda is one of the easier group trips in Africa. Kigali is clean and calm after dark by regional standards, roads between the main sights are paved, and a private driver-guide stays with your group. Take the usual city precautions with phones and bags.

How many days do you need for a girls trip to Rwanda?

Seven days is the sweet spot for a girls trip to Rwanda: two nights in Kigali, two or three near Volcanoes National Park and two on Lake Kivu. Five days covers Kigali and the gorillas only, while nine or ten adds Akagera or Nyungwe without rushing.

How much does a girls trip to Rwanda cost?

A seven-day girls trip to Rwanda costs roughly US$3,000 to US$4,000 per person in comfortable mid-range hotels, US$4,500 to US$6,500 in upper mid-range lodges, and US$9,000 or more in top luxury lodges, sharing rooms and a private vehicle. These are estimates; the US$1,500 gorilla permit is the largest single item.

Can friends who do not want to trek gorillas still come?

Yes. Friends who skip the gorilla trek can still enjoy a girls trip to Rwanda. While the others trek, they can join golden monkey tracking, visit a community or cultural village near Musanze, take a spa morning at the lodge or explore the area with a guide. The group then meets up again for lunch.

Do we need a visa for Rwanda?

Most visitors can get a Rwanda visa on arrival at Kigali airport. Citizens of African Union, Commonwealth and La Francophonie countries have the fee waived for a 30-day visit, and the single-entry fee for others is capped at US$50 (Rwanda Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, checked November 2026). Confirm your nationality's rules before you fly.

Final Thoughts

A girls trip to Rwanda works best as a week of contrasts: Kigali's cafés and history, an unforgettable hour with the gorillas, and two easy days on Lake Kivu to talk it all over. Book permits early, agree the budget tier as a group and keep one free afternoon.
